correspondence.finding: The northwestern beginning bends east and south, then turns east through the western lake approach. The MRNF sheet places Lac Boivin west of Lac Maublant and the retained CEHQ sheet labels the associated Boivin feeder corridor. This supports the western approach; the exact hydronym of the initial small selected feeder is not established.

The eastward connection reaches Maublant and turns southeast through Plétipi toward the Lac des Îles Brûlées outlet setting. MDDEP’s detailed hydrographic map distinguishes this western lake entry from the separate northern river inlet labeled Rivière aux Outardes. The source lake, intervening lake passages and downstream river therefore retain separate naming scope.

Below the Plétipi lake country, the selected corridor continues southeast and then south along the named Rivière aux Outardes, remaining west of Réservoir Manicouagan. Matonipi is a separately mapped eastern tributary basin; the selection does not follow its upper lake branch or the Manicouagan trunk.

The middle-to-lower route enters the long north–south Réservoir Outardes 4 corridor before turning southeast into the lower river. The CEHQ and MDDEP maps separately depict Outardes 4, Pipmuacan to the west and Manic 3/Manic 2 to the east; the selected line does not switch into those neighboring reservoir systems. The river-system identity does not rename the reservoir as a natural river reach.

The selected final approach is in the lower Outardes-2 vicinity southwest of Baie-Comeau. The provincial technical record locates the east dike and identifies its reservoir and watercourse as Outardes 2 and Rivière aux Outardes. The regional maps show the wider downstream connection to the Saint-Laurent. The selected endpoint is not asserted to be a dam crest, a surveyed mouth, a tidal limit or the full estuarine channel.

The first modeled-mainstem piece approaches Barra do Corda from the west, north of the officially mapped upper Mearim. CPRM maps the Capim Duro/Cipó feeder setting on this northern side, while its explicitly labeled Rio Mearim follows the southern São Pedro–Arranca corridor. The selected approach is therefore retained as a headward feeder complex; neither the whole piece nor its start is asserted to be the natural upper Mearim. Exact feeder-name transitions remain unassigned.

From Barra do Corda the selected trunk turns northeast toward the Santa Vitória and Esperantinópolis setting, then bends east toward the Flores junction region. ANA maps this route separately from the southern Corda/Capim and Flores contributions. SEMA explicitly assigns Barra do Corda and Santa Vitória stations to Mearim and Joselândia to Flores; Flores is not a replacement name for the selected trunk.

The middle pieces turn north through Pedreiras, westward through the São Luiz Gonzaga–Bacabal setting and then northeast toward the lower river. The IBGE and ANA maps show this distinctive sequence; SEMA directly identifies Pedreiras II, São Luiz Gonzaga and Bacabal stations on Mearim. The eastern Itapecuru corridor is separate.

The three western contribution pieces rise from the southern headward setting, pass Grajaú, turn northeast past Itaipava do Grajaú and continue north to the Aratoí Grande setting before joining the selected eastern trunk. Official maps identify the main contributing corridor as Rio Grajaú; SEMA assigns Grajaú II and Aratoí Grande stations to Grajaú. Its extreme southern feeder name and the final joining-channel name remain unassigned. This long contribution is not renamed Mearim or Pindaré.

After the western contribution joins, the short final piece continues north through the inland Arari–Vitória do Mearim setting. The mapped Mearim and coastal network continue beyond the selected endpoint, while Pindaré approaches separately from the west. No Atlantic mouth, estuary, tidal boundary or complete lower floodplain network is assigned to this truncated selection.

The northern approach matches the Huevachi/eastern Ocampo setting and the southward channel near the Uruachi–Maguarichi boundary. Municipal maps distinguish the Maguarichi and Oteros branches; neither name is assigned wholesale to this initial feeder.

Below the Uruachi setting, the selected westward and southwestward course follows the lower Oteros corridor and then turns south past Chínipas de Almada. The separate Mayo drainage lies to the west; municipal basin membership alone was not used to choose the identity.

The southward Chínipas approach reaches the Septentrión junction and the northern arm of Luis Donaldo Colosio Murrieta (Huites). The separately mapped Río Fuerte approach from the east is not the selected upstream branch.

Below Huites, the route bends west through the Agua Caliente de Baca setting and south through Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla (El Mahone) toward El Fuerte. Josefa Ortiz de Domínguez storage is separately mapped to the west and is not traversed by this selected course.

The lower course continues south through the San Blas setting, turns west across the San Miguel Zapotitlán–El Guayabo plain and approaches the coast near Las Grullas and Boca las Piedras. The maps distinguish the river corridor from the surrounding canal grid; no exact current mouth, shoreline or distributary extent is asserted.

correspondence: The complete three-piece selected mainstem was inspected, including the long north-northwest interior leg, westward undulating middle corridor, abrupt western southward turn and winding western ending. There is no separately selected tributary piece.

The long eastern and middle portions lie on mapped Inland Ice. The western portion approaches the ice margin and adjoining inland terrain in the broader Isukasia region, east of Maniitsoq and north of Nuuk. The map graticule and surrounding ice/land arrangement support regional correspondence, but no exact terminal stream, lake or glacier boundary is assigned.

The map does not establish the complete modeled line as a named natural river or glacier. Western marginal waterways cannot supply a uniform hydronym for the extensive interior-ice path, and the scope hold does not assert that every local marginal stream is unnamed.

The legend distinguishes ice-surface, thickness and sub-ice bedrock contours. In this southern region, bold blue aeromagnetic lineaments are also present and are not river channels. Historical mapping establishes neither present-day ice margins nor flow or subglacial connectivity along the selected line.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
